name: straus_exponent_budget

phase_0.boundary_condition: The modulus r coprime to M, which bounds the units group (Z/rZ)* and contains both the subgroup generated by primes dividing M and the image of divisors of M squared modulo r

VINIT.chosen_element: The empty register before any prime exponent is assigned or any generator is selected
VINIT.justification: Before the system can compare the two sets, no prime has been chosen, no exponent has been read, and no element of (Z/rZ)* has been generated. This is the void state 00.

TANCH.chosen_element: The modulus r coprime to M, defining the finite boundary of the units group (Z/rZ)*
TANCH.justification: The modulus r is the terminal anchor that closes and contains the entire system. All generators, exponents, and images live within (Z/rZ)*, and r itself is the boundary that makes the comparison finite and well-defined.

AFWD.chosen_element: The forward morphism from a prime p dividing M to its exponent e_p, then to the generator p^{e_p} in (Z/rZ)*
AFWD.justification: The system advances from the prime factorization of M through the exponent available to each prime, producing a generator in the multiplicative subgroup. This is the directed transformation toward the target set.

AREV.chosen_element: The reverse morphism from the image of divisors of M squared back to the exponent data of each prime
AREV.justification: The system descends from the image set (divisors of M squared modulo r) back to the exponent structure that produced it. This parity flip belongs on the F-arm, recovering the exponent data from the image.

CLINK.chosen_element: The sequential chaining of prime exponent extraction, subgroup generation, and image computation
CLINK.justification: The system composes the steps: extract exponents from M, generate the subgroup from primes, compute the image from divisors of M squared, and compare. Each step is a morphism chained to the next.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: The self-referential comparison of the two sets against each other
IMSCRIB.justification: The object measures the difference between the subgroup and the image by recognizing itself in both: the same exponent data feeds both constructions, and the comparison is a self-recognition of whether they coincide.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The bifurcation of the exponent data into the multiplicative subgroup generator path and the divisor image path
FSPLIT.justification: The central quantity, the exponent available to each prime, splits into two arms: one arm generates the multiplicative subgroup of (Z/rZ)* from primes dividing M, and the other arm computes the image of divisors of M squared modulo r.

FFUSE.chosen_element: The rejoining of the subgroup and image paths into a single comparison verdict
FFUSE.justification: The two arms, after computing the subgroup and the image respectively, rejoin into one state: the difference or coincidence of the two sets. Conflicting arms (subgroup ≠ image) rejoin to B, a paradice holding both the affirmation and the deficiency.

EVALT.chosen_element: The affirmative state where the multiplicative subgroup equals the image of divisors of M squared modulo r
EVALT.justification: When the two sets coincide, the T-arm affirms that the exponent-based construction yields identical results on both paths. This is the constructive truth of equality.

EVALF.chosen_element: The negative state where the multiplicative subgroup does not equal the image of divisors of M squared modulo r
EVALF.justification: When the two sets differ, the F-arm refutes equality and establishes the deficiency. This is the constructive falsity of non-coincidence.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The paradice state where the two sets both coincide and differ simultaneously, or where the comparison is undecidable within the given modulus
ENGAGR.justification: At the critical case where μ∘δ=id is provably exact, the system may hold both the affirmation of coincidence and the refutation of deficiency at once. This is the B-state, a contradiction kept live without resolution.

IFIX.chosen_element: The permanent record of the computed difference or coincidence for a specific (M, r) pair
IFIX.justification: Once the comparison is made, the result is fixed as an append-only record. The verdict for a given M and r cannot be undone; it is a measurement record.

phase_2.split_element: FSPLIT: the exponent data of primes dividing M bifurcates into subgroup generation and divisor image computation
phase_2.split_input: The exponent available to each prime dividing M, extracted from the prime factorization of M
split_outputs: The multiplicative subgroup of (Z/rZ)* generated by primes dividing M, using exponents e_p
The image modulo r of the divisors of M squared, using exponents 2*e_p
phase_2.fuse_element: FFUSE: the subgroup and image paths rejoin into a single comparison state
phase_2.fuse_result: A single B4 verdict: T if the two sets coincide, F if they differ, B if both states are held simultaneously (paradice), N if no comparison was established
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Register 00: no prime exponent has been read, no generator selected, no element of (Z/rZ)* produced. The system is uninitialized.
phase_3.true_description: Register 01: the multiplicative subgroup generated by primes dividing M equals the image of divisors of M squared modulo r. The exponent-based construction yields identical sets.
phase_3.false_description: Register 10: the multiplicative subgroup and the image of divisors of M squared modulo r are distinct. A deficiency exists, measured by the symmetric difference of the two sets.
phase_3.both_description: Register 11: the system holds both the affirmation of coincidence and the refutation of deficiency simultaneously. This paradice state arises at the critical Frobenius case where μ∘δ=id is exact, or when the comparison is structurally undecidable.

steps.domain_action: The system begins in the void state, before any prime exponent is assigned or any generator is selected from the units group (Z/rZ)*.
The prime factorization of M is processed, extracting the exponent e_p available to each prime p dividing M.
The forward morphism maps each prime p and its exponent e_p to the generator p^{e_p} in the multiplicative subgroup of (Z/rZ)*.
The exponent data bifurcates into two arms: the T-arm generates the subgroup from primes dividing M, and the F-arm computes the image from divisors of M squared.
The T-arm affirms that the multiplicative subgroup generated by primes dividing M, using exponents e_p, produces a well-defined subset of (Z/rZ)*.
The F-arm refutes coincidence by computing the image of divisors of M squared modulo r, using exponents 2*e_p, and establishing the deficiency when the sets differ.
At the critical case where μ∘δ=id is provably exact, the system holds both the affirmation of coincidence and the refutation of deficiency simultaneously as a paradice state.
The two arms rejoin into a single B4 verdict over SIXTEEN_3: T if the sets coincide, F if they differ, B if both are held, N if no comparison was established.
The reverse morphism descends from the image set back to the exponent data, recovering the exponent structure that produced the image from divisors of M squared.
The comparison result is composed with the modulus r boundary, closing the system within the finite units group (Z/rZ)*.
The self-referential comparison recognizes that the same exponent data feeds both constructions, and the object measures its own difference by comparing the two paths.
The computed verdict for the specific (M, r) pair is permanently recorded as an append-only measurement, fixing the result without possibility of reversal.
The modulus r serves as the terminal anchor, closing and containing the entire system within the finite boundary of (Z/rZ)*.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The exponent extraction engine that reads the prime factorization of M and produces the exponent e_p for each prime p dividing M, then maps these to generators in (Z/rZ)*
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The units group (Z/rZ)* serves as the shared communication channel: both the subgroup and the image are computed as subsets of this group, and their comparison is the inter-process message.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The register state (00/01/10/11) stores the current B4 verdict, while the IFIX records maintain a permanent append-only log of all (M, r) comparisons made.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The modulus r determines the order and timing: all computations occur within the finite group (Z/rZ)*, and the comparison is scheduled once both the subgroup and image have been fully generated.
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical reference is the Frobenius closure condition μ∘δ=id, which defines the critical case where the multiplicative subgroup and the image of divisors of M squared coincide exactly.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The computational cost of generating elements in (Z/rZ)*, computing the subgroup from prime generators, and computing the image from divisors of M squared modulo r
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The system holds the prime factorization of M and the modulus r coprime to M, with no sets yet generated or compared.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The system holds the B4 verdict (T, F, B, or N) representing the relationship between the multiplicative subgroup and the image of divisors of M squared modulo r, with the result permanently fixed in an IFIX record.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system operates within the finite group (Z/rZ)*, where all computations are bounded. The comparison is a measurement of structure, not a creation of disorder. The IFIX record preserves the result without dissipation, and the modulus r provides a closed boundary that prevents entropy leakage.

banked_count_check.verdict: 4 unit(s) of weight cleared with nothing banked behind them: the count was in the open when the reversal came
banked_count_check.remedy: open the region that holds the result BEFORE the region that computes it, and close them in that order, so the inner fuse folds into the enclosing frame rather than into the register
